title: Eliana T
content: THIS IS MY TESTIMONY IN STORY VERSION. Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a young girl named Lisa. She was cheerful and curious, and she loved hearing her papa’s stories about Jesus, an extraordinary God who performed miracles. Her papa told her about healing a man who could not walk, describing how the man leaped from his wheelchair and ran joyfully after being healed. He spoke of a blind man whose milky white eyes transformed into beautiful brown ones in an instant. But the most incredible story was when her father’s heart stopped beating, and he stood in the presence of Jesus in a place of breathtaking beauty. There, he could run effortlessly, surrounded by colors unseen on Earth, walking along paths of gold. Jesus gently urged him to step on a flower. Though hesitant, he obeyed. To his amazement, the flower instantly sprang back to life. Nothing withered in that place because, as Jesus explained, He was its everlasting light. Lisa’s father had unwavering faith, and his stories inspired her deeply. Between the ages of 9 and 11, she prayed nightly, asking God, "Let me see you as my papa did, but without dying. I want unshakable faith in you." Over time, she forgot those prayers. At 16, Lisa worked at a Christian camp, leading children on adventures such as archery in the forest, canoe rides across the lake, and flying fox rides. Laughter filled the air until one tragic day. After the other children left, Lisa and her friend Aimee took a go-kart for a spin. Lisa drove, racing around the track with laughter ringing out. Then disaster struck. The kart veered off course as it climbed a hill, flipping over and trapping Lisa underneath. People rushed to help. Aimee was shaken but unharmed, while Lisa lay motionless, unable to speak, her body cold. Jenny, the camp leader, called an ambulance. As they waited, Jenny tried to warm Lisa with blankets and reassured her as best she could. Forty agonizing minutes passed before the paramedics arrived. When they touched Lisa’s shoulders, she fainted, and darkness swallowed her. On the way to the hospital, a paramedic realized Lisa’s heart had stopped. Panic set in. The ambulance pulled over while both medics worked frantically and called ahead to urge the hospital to prepare. For ten harrowing minutes, Lisa showed no signs of life. Miraculously, they revived her. At the hospital, friends and family waited in dread. Lisa’s parents arrived, fearing another broken bone, only to hear a nurse’s devastating words: "Come say goodbye." Lisa was losing too much blood. Her liver was split, and her arteries were damaged beyond repair. Her father, furious and heartbroken, stormed outside and cried out to God. He shouted, "After all my years serving you, you take my daughter? You can’t do this!" Then, softly, a voice answered him. It asked, "Do you not trust me?" Trembling, he rushed back inside and told the nurse, "Open Lisa up, pack her with towels, and wrap her in plastic." The nurses hesitated but obeyed. Hours later, they returned in awe. The towels had slowed the bleeding enough to stabilize her so she could be moved to Auckland Hospital. Surgeons even canceled their plans to help because she was stable. Grateful and weeping, Lisa’s parents praised God and trusted His power even in their despair. Meanwhile, Lisa found herself in darkness. Voices echoed around her, but she saw nothing until a pinpoint of light grew larger, illuminating golden gates adorned with pearls. Peace enveloped her as she reached out to open them. But then a hand rested on her shoulder. A voice told her, "Stop. You cannot go in." She turned and saw God, radiant and immense. He said, "Walk with me." Hand in hand, He explained, "You cannot stay. I have work for you to do." As she returned, giant green leaves unlike any on Earth drifted around her. Then she awoke in a hospital bed to her father whispering, "Welcome back." Lisa knew God was real. Recovery was grueling. She had to relearn to walk, and her scar became a constant reminder of His presence. She shared her story at churches and camp. Many people told her, "Your faith restored mine." One day, she knows she will see those gates again. Until then, she continues to tell her story, spreading hope. My name is Eliana. Months after my recovery, I felt drawn to my middle name. At the time, I didn’t know its meaning: "God has answered me." And He truly had. Rev 21:23 – The city does not need the sun or moon to shine, for the glory of God gives it light. Rev 22:2 – On each side of the river stands the tree of life, with leaves for the healing of the nations.

diagnosis.diagnosis_raw: Traumatic injuries after go-kart accident: losing too much blood; liver split; arteries damaged beyond repair; heart stopped.
diagnosis.disease_name: Severe traumatic hemorrhage with liver laceration and arterial injury; cardiac arrest
diagnosis.severity_description: Life-threatening hemorrhage; told parents 'Come say goodbye'; 10 minutes with no signs of life in ambulance
diagnosis.quality_of_life_impact: Had to relearn to walk; prolonged/grueling recovery
diagnosis.disease_duration_before_healing: Acute traumatic event (same day as accident)
diagnosis.mobility_status: Unable to walk normally initially; had to relearn to walk during recovery
diagnosis.vascular_condition: Arteries damaged; severe bleeding; cardiac arrest in ambulance

treatment.treatments_raw: Ambulance resuscitation after heart stopped; emergency hospital intervention; instructed nurses to open her up, pack her with towels, and wrap her in plastic; later transferred to Auckland Hospital; surgeons involved/planned.
treatment.surgery_type: Emergency opening/packing/wrapping for hemorrhage control (as described)
treatment.surgery_outcome: Bleeding slowed enough to stabilize for transfer; surgeons canceled plans to help because she was stable

remission_outcome.verification_detail: Narrative reports paramedics noted cardiac arrest and revived her; hospital staff stated she was losing too much blood with liver split/arterial damage; later 'towels had slowed the bleeding enough to stabilize her' enabling transfer; she survived and later relearned to walk.
remission_outcome.follow_up_duration_raw: Months after recovery (name meaning realization); long-term survival implied

intuition_examples: Father heard a voice asking 'Do you not trust me?' and then instructed staff to open her up, pack with towels, and wrap in plastic
turner_factors.intuition_details: Guidance/voice leading to a specific action described as pivotal to stabilizing bleeding.
positive_emotion_practices: Sharing testimony to inspire others' faith
turner_factors.spiritual_practices_raw: Prayed nightly as a child; later shared testimony at churches; strong Christian faith focus on Jesus/God.
purpose_sources: Belief that God said 'I have work for you to do'
Spreading hope/restoring others' faith by telling her story
turner_factors.purpose_details: Returned from experience believing she had work to do and continued to share testimony.

pre_illness_state.pre_illness_description: Cheerful/curious youth; strong Christian exposure via father; worked at a Christian camp.

existential_shift.identity_shift_description: After the experience, she 'knew God was real' and oriented life around testimony/faith.
existential_shift.surrender_description: Family moved from anger/despair to trust in God; she accepted returning because 'You cannot stay. I have work for you to do.'
existential_shift.transformation_narrative: Near-death experience led to certainty of God's reality and a life focused on sharing hope/faith.
existential_shift.pivot_point_description: In the experience, told by God she could not enter the gates and must return because there was work to do.
existential_shift.transformation_timing: Experience occurred during period of cardiac arrest/critical injury, before awakening and subsequent recovery.
major_life_changes: Began sharing her testimony at churches and camp

anomalous_experience.experience_description: Darkness followed by growing light; golden gates with pearls; a hand stopped her; she saw God radiant and immense; told she could not stay and had work to do; returned seeing giant green leaves unlike Earth.
anomalous_experience.experience_timing: During ambulance transport/period when heart stopped and she was critically injured
anomalous_experience.message_content: “You cannot stay. I have work for you to do.”

correspondential_markers.correspondence_notes: Narrative centers on faith/trust and a near-death experience rather than pre-illness ego/resentment patterns.
correspondential_markers.resolution_type: Trust/surrender to God; receiving directive to return and live with purpose

validation.statistical_improbability_notes: Survival described despite being told to say goodbye, massive bleeding, and ~10 minutes with no signs of life; however, substantial emergency medical intervention occurred.
validation.extraction_notes: This is not a spontaneous remission case but a trauma/NDE survival narrative. Many clinical specifics (imaging, exact procedures, dates) are not provided.

analysis.case_summary: A 16-year-old female suffered a severe go-kart accident with massive hemorrhage (split liver, arterial damage) and cardiac arrest en route to hospital. During the critical period she reports an NDE with a message to return because she had work to do; she survived after emergency interventions and later underwent a difficult recovery, relearning to walk.
key_healing_factors: Emergency resuscitation and hemorrhage-control measures described (packing with towels/wrapping; stabilization for transfer)
Strong Christian faith and prayer (patient and family)
Near-death experience with a directive to return and live with purpose
Strong family/community support and meaning-making through testimony
unique_features: Explicit NDE with golden gates and encounter with God
Father reports hearing a voice prompting trust and a specific action that allegedly helped stabilize bleeding
Hospital transfer to Auckland Hospital mentioned
analysis.analysis_notes: The narrative frames survival as miraculous, but the described outcome follows emergency medical care for trauma rather than disease remission. Remission fields are populated as applicable to survival/recovery, but no cancer/autoimmune/infectious illness is present.
